newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Q1 yr/yr GDP 4.8 pct vs 0.6 pct Q1 1996.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Q1 yr/yr GDP 4.8 pct vs 0.6 pct Q1 1996.

text.p: The Peruvian economy grew 4.8 percent year-on-year in the first quarter, compared with a 0.6 percent year-on-year growth in the January to March period of 1996, the government's statistics agency said Monday.
Earlier the National Institute of Statistics and Information (INEI) said year-on-year Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in March was 5.2 percent, compared with a 0.9 contraction in March last year.

The country's first quarter year-on-year growth was led by the agriculture sector at 14.4 percent, followed by construction with 9.8 percent, the INEI said, without giving comparative figures for the first quarter 1996.
The worst performing sector in the first quarter was fishing, which contracted 12.2 percent.

Among other sectors, commerce grew 5.0 percent, electricity and water was up 4.3 percent and the INEI's category for "others," including the transport, financial and government sectors, rose 3.4 percent. The manufacturing sector grew 2.7 percent and mining gained 1.6 percent.

The country's March year-on-year growth was led by the fishing sector at 36.6 percent, followed by agriculture with 11.7 percent, the INEI said, without giving comparative figures for the first quarter 1996.
The worst performing sector in March was mining, which grew 1.4 percent.

Among other sectors in March, manufacturing grew 5.2 percent, commerce 5.2 percent and electricity and water 5.1 percent. The INEI's category for "others," rose 3.9 percent and the construction sector grew 3.1 percent.
The government estimates Peru is headed for overall GDP growth of four to five percent in 1997.
Peru's GDP rose 2.8 percent in 1996 versus 7.0 percent the previous year.

GDP figures provided by the INEI often differ slightly from those of the central bank, which are published later, because the bank collects additional information from the country's customs agency SUNAD, according to bank officials.
